text:
Alice Chen: FYI customer (enterprise account) reports sudden p95/p99 latency spikes in the last 30m after a config push. They see long queueing delays (200-800ms extra) and some 429s for high-concurrency bursts. sending their simplified repro below.

Marco Ruiz: thanks Alice. any ETA on repro steps from the customer? also which cluster/region?

Alice Chen: their app targets eu-west-1 hosted endpoints. Repro steps they provided: 1) open 50 concurrent connections 2) send 1 request per connection every 600ms for ~2 minutes 3) observe p95 jump from ~80ms to ~450-700ms, and occasional 429s. They shared a curl loop and a small load generator.

Priya Nair: I started looking at runtime metrics — looks like request queue length spiked on the gateway/proxy layer around the same time as a recent canary rollout. KV cache misses also increased. Could be admission control kicking in or an overloaded worker pool.

Darren (oncall): deploy-bot shows a canary config change at 1865432080 for router-concurrency defaults. deploy-bot: "canary apply: router-config v17 -> v18 (rollout 5%)"

Grace Li: that rings a bell — product requested a default concurrency increase to reduce throttling for small requests, but config had a bug that didn't propagate admission limits to backend pools. Might explain backlog at the gateway while workers didn't scale.

Marco Ruiz: pulling metrics: gateway ingress p99 latency and pending queue length. From 1865432060 to 1865432120 queue depth jumped from ~3 to ~220 for a subset of routes. Worker utilization stayed high (~95%) and autoscaler didn't kick because pod concurrency limit reached.

Priya Nair: logs show repeated lines on a few workers: "serve: admission deny - concurrency limit reached" and then later many requests queued inside the router:

```
2026-03-15T10:05:23Z router/conn=12345 queued=178 route=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T10:05:24Z worker/abc123 serve start seq=987
2026-03-15T10:05:24Z worker/abc123 kvcache miss model=gpt-xx
2026-03-15T10:05:25Z router/conn=12345 admit retry backoff=50ms
```

Priya Nair: also saw an increase in long tail GPU context switch times — potentially due to small-batch inefficiency after the canary changed kernel flags.

Alice Chen: customer is blocked — they have production traffic. They asked for a mitigation ASAP. Can we do a quick rollback of the canary or route their traffic to a separate pool?

Darren (oncall): immediate options: 1) roll back router-config to v17 2) open emergency override to raise worker concurrency temporarily 3) move their account to dedicated pool if available. Which is fastest?

Marco Ruiz: fastest is rollback of canary to v17. That should restore previous admission behavior. I can trigger rollback and watch queue depth. Priya, any risk with rollback?

Priya Nair: rollback safe for routing config; it won't touch model binaries. However, we should also clear pending queued requests to avoid long tails — but router will drain gracefully. I'll prepare a temporary autoscaler override if rollback doesn't fully fix it.

Grace Li: I'm patching the config bug in staging now so we don't reintroduce this. The bug is: missing propagation of per-worker concurrency quotas when router-level concurrency was increased. Fix will be a small change to ensure worker-level admission inherits router overrides.

Marco Ruiz: initiating rollback now. deploy-bot: "canary rollback: router-config v18 -> v17 (rollback initiated by Marco)"

LogWatcher Bot: alert suppressed: p95 latency for route /v1/generate now trending down (was 670ms, now 130ms). Previous alert: p95-p99-latency-euw1.

Darren (oncall): monitoring SLA windows — keep me posted if p99 stays elevated for another 15m. If rollback doesn't fully recover, we'll do an autoscaler override and consider a temporary routing rule to send this customer's traffic to a less-burdened region.

Alice Chen: told customer we rolled back the canary and are monitoring. They confirmed seeing immediate improvement on their end.

Priya Nair: after rollback, queue depth dropped back to baseline (~4-7) and worker load normalized to ~60-70%. p99 down to ~150ms. Verified KV cache hit-rate improved for that model region.

Marco Ruiz: leaving the thread open for 30m to watch for regressions. I'll follow up with a postmortem and include mitigation checklist: - avoid partial router-only concurrency increases without worker propagation - add guard in rollout pipeline to validate worker-level admission unchanged - add synthetic test to simulate bursty concurrency 50x50 for 2m during canary.

Grace Li: opened a ticket (ENG-5241) to backport the fix and add the rollout gate.

Darren (oncall): resolution tentative — rollback successful and customer reports normal latency. If anything flares up ping me on-call.

Alice Chen: customer thanked us and will keep us updated. Marking as resolved from support side pending postmortem. :thumbsup:
